purpose: Held-out proof that generic grouped derivation and ranked selection IR generalizes across different entities, relation fields, copied fields, and scalar filter types.
goal: Using a real rendered browser, open https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts, save a screenshot to canonical/astra_runtime/tmp/RANK_POSTS.png, and save the rendered result to canonical/astra_runtime/tmp/RANK_POSTS.json. Using a real rendered browser, open https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/comments, save a screenshot to canonical/astra_runtime/tmp/RANK_COMMENTS.png, and save the rendered result to canonical/astra_runtime/tmp/RANK_COMMENTS.json. Using both live results, create canonical/astra_runtime/tmp/POST_COMMENT_RATES.json containing exactly one record per live post with post_id, title, total_count, matched_count, and match_ratio, where total_count is the number of live comments whose postId equals that post's id, matched_count is the number of those comments whose email field is Eliseo@gardner.biz, and match_ratio is matched_count divided by total_count. From canonical/astra_runtime/tmp/POST_COMMENT_RATES.json select exactly one winner with the greatest match_ratio, breaking ties by the lowest post_id, and save canonical/astra_runtime/tmp/POST_COMMENT_WINNER.json containing post_id, title, total_count, matched_count, and match_ratio. Finally independently reopen both live source results, canonical/astra_runtime/tmp/POST_COMMENT_RATES.json, and canonical/astra_runtime/tmp/POST_COMMENT_WINNER.json and verify every post's counts and match_ratio are correct, the winner has the greatest match_ratio, the lowest post_id wins any tie, every live post appears exactly once in the rates file, and there are no extra records.
